title: TaL: a synchronised multi-speaker corpus of ultrasound tongue imaging, audio, and lip videos
why_promising: Primary non-singing English production with synchronised audio, raw ultrasound tongue imaging, lip video and hardware synchronisation from 82 speakers (TaL1 plus TaL80), approximately 24 hours overall / 13.5 hours speech. Public documentation states that long spontaneous-speech utterances have manually annotated short-segment boundaries with start/end times and transcription, and participant/session metadata are distributed with the corpus. The corpus is publicly downloadable and documented as CC BY-NC 4.0. This is a high-value articulatory source because the primary imaging/audio streams can be linked to manual temporal segmentation without reducing trajectories to midpoint summaries.
open_question: Before core promotion, enumerate the TaL1/TaL80 doc and annotation CSV files at file level, verify which boundary/transcription files are manual versus automatic, inventory participant metadata and synchronization semantics, and determine whether any manually verified phone/word landmarks or derived tongue/lip measurements are distributed. Avoid mirroring the ~547 GB raw core streams to GitHub; retain authoritative paths/checksums and ingest redistributable annotations/metadata plus derived structured measurements only.

title: The MRPL2 Non-native Speech Corpus
why_promising: Primary non-singing L2 English production: 4,500 utterances from 23 non-native speakers representing 14 L1s. The Zenodo record states that every utterance was manually annotated for phonetic mispronunciations relative to Modern Received Pronunciation and that annotated TextGrids, word transcripts, 48/16-kHz audio, and corpus-wide expected versus ground-truth phoneme sequence master files are included. This directly targets L2 phonetics, categorical production errors, segment context and pronunciation outcomes.
open_question: Files are currently restricted behind Zenodo request access. Keep out of core until authorized file-level access is available and license/redistribution terms can be recorded. If access is obtained, inventory every TextGrid/master file, preserve expected and ground-truth sequences separately, namespace speaker/utterance/token IDs, and ingest manual error labels and boundaries without treating any automatic alignments as human annotations.
